opportunities.title: Crypto's First Quantum Hack Won't Announce Itself — It'll Just Look Like a Stolen Key
opportunities.why_now: A Quantus founder is warning that quantum theft will be indistinguishable from ordinary key compromise, right as the industry treats quantum risk as science fiction.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/thesis piece connecting the quantum warning to real 'unexplained' wallet drains — end with a checklist of what would actually look different forensically.

opportunities.title: The Coldcard Hack Is Solved by Chain Forensics, Not Better Hardware
opportunities.why_now: New reporting details exactly how investigators traced the stolen Coldcard funds, offering a rare inside look at post-breach recovery mechanics.
opportunities.angle: Breakdown/explainer of the tracing methodology, framed as 'here's what actually happens after your hardware wallet gets popped' — pairs incident detail with hard lessons on custody.

opportunities.title: BTCPay Just Locked Down Remote Lightning Access — Translation: It Was Always the Weak Point
opportunities.why_now: BTCPay restricted remote Lightning access and posted a $190K bounty within days of attackers draining self-hosted payment servers.
opportunities.angle: Incident postmortem for self-custody infra operators — what changed, why it should've been the default from day one, and a quick self-audit checklist for anyone running BTCPay.

opportunities.title: Coinsbuy's $8M Breach Across Two Chains Is the Multi-Chain Custody Problem Nobody Wants to Solve
opportunities.why_now: Coinsbuy confirmed wallets were drained across two blockchains and is now offering a $100K reward, a live case study in cross-chain custodial failure.
opportunities.angle: Analysis piece on why multi-chain support multiplies attack surface for exchanges, using Coinsbuy as the cautionary example — tie to broader exchange security posture.

opportunities.title: A Bitcoin Wallet Just Woke Up After 12 Years — Cold Storage Was Never 'Set and Forget'
opportunities.why_now: Another long-dormant wallet holding millions just moved, reviving the recurring question of what happens to keys nobody's touched in over a decade.
opportunities.angle: Short, punchy piece on key custody hygiene over long time horizons — inheritance, hardware obsolescence, and why 'buy and forget' is a security anti-pattern, not a strategy.
